item.title: Elder Nādīkassapa: Truly it was beneficial for me that the Buddha came here, To the river called Nerañjarā. I heard his teaching, and my wrong…
item.description:
Elder Nādīkassapa:

Truly it was beneficial for me that the Buddha came here,
To the river called Nerañjarā.
I heard his teaching, and my wrong views were destroyed.

I performed sacrifices, recited sacrificial chants,
I kindled the sacred fire, poured offerings into the fire,
Thinking I was purified — truly I was a blind worldling.

Wandering in the forest of wrong views, blinded by rites and rituals,
Not pure, thinking I was pure — blind, I did not see.

I have destroyed wrong views, broken all existence,
I kindle the fire, worthy of offerings,
I bow down in homage to the Tathāgata, the Tamer.

All delusion is destroyed, craving for existence is shattered,
The path of birth and death is cut off; now there is no more renewed existence.

From: Theragāthā 5.6

item.title: Here, friends, while I was alone in seclusion, the following thought arose in my mind: 'Noble silence, noble silence is said. What is noble silence?'…
item.description:
Here, friends, while I was alone in seclusion, the following thought arose in my mind: 'Noble silence, noble silence is said. What is noble silence?' Then, friends, I thought: 'Here, a bhikkhu, with the stilling of initial and sustained thought, enters and abides in the second jhāna, which has internal clarity and unification of mind, without initial and sustained thought, with rapture and happiness born of concentration. This is called noble silence.' Then, friends, I, with the stilling of initial and sustained thought, entered and abided in the second jhāna. Friends, while I abided in this abiding, perceptions and attention accompanied by thought arose and persisted. Then, friends, the Blessed One, by psychic power, came to me and said: 'Moggallāna, Moggallāna, do not be heedless, brahmin. Regarding noble silence, establish your mind in noble silence, unify your mind in noble silence, concentrate your mind in noble silence.' Then, friends, after some time, I, with the stilling of initial and sustained thought, entered and abided in the second jhāna. Friends, one speaking rightly would say: 'The disciple attained great direct knowledge through the Teacher's assistance.' Speaking rightly, one would say of me: 'The disciple attained great direct knowledge through the Teacher's assistance.'

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 21.1

item.title: Here, bhikkhus, knowing a person's mind as defiled with my own mind, I understand: 'If this person were to die at this time, he would…
item.description:
Here, bhikkhus, knowing a person's mind as defiled with my own mind, I understand: 'If this person were to die at this time, he would be reborn in hell accordingly.' Why is that? Because his mind is defiled. It is because of a defiled mind, bhikkhus, that some beings here, after death, with the breakup of the body, are reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.43

item.title: Bhikkhus, how does a bhikkhu practice the things proper to a samaṇa? He abides pervading one direction with a mind imbued with loving-kindness... compassion... altruistic…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, how does a bhikkhu practice the things proper to a samaṇa? He abides pervading one direction with a mind imbued with loving-kindness... compassion... altruistic joy... equanimity, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, across, everywhere, in all respects, he abides pervading the entire world with a mind imbued with equanimity, vast, immeasurable, without hostility, without ill-will. Bhikkhus, just as a lotus pond with clear, sweet, cool, limpid water, with beautifully arranged banks, is delightful — if a person comes from the east, overcome and afflicted by heat, exhausted, parched, and thirsty, and goes to that pond, he would quench his thirst and cool his heat... if a person comes from the west... from the north... from the south... from anywhere, overcome by heat, afflicted, exhausted, parched, and thirsty, and goes to that pond, he would quench his thirst and cool his heat. So too, bhikkhus, if a person from the noble warrior caste goes forth from home to homelessness and comes to the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata, and having developed loving-kindness, compassion, altruistic joy, and equanimity, attains inner concentration — I say that through this inner concentration he practices the things proper to a samaṇa.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 40 – Cūḷaassapurasutta

item.title: Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu reviles, criticizes, or reproaches the noble ones who are his fellow celibates, it is impossible, there is no chance that he…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu reviles, criticizes, or reproaches the noble ones who are his fellow celibates, it is impossible, there is no chance that he will not encounter one of eleven misfortunes. What eleven? He does not attain what has not been attained; what has been attained he loses; the true Dhamma is not made clear to him; or he becomes puffed up in the true Dhamma; or he does not delight in living the holy life; or he commits a defiled offense; or he gives up the holy life and returns to the lower life; or he contracts a severe illness; or he becomes mad or mentally deranged; or he dies confused; or after death, with the breakup of the body, he falls into a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell. Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu reviles, criticizes, or reproaches the noble ones who are his fellow celibates, it is impossible, there is no chance that he will not encounter one of these eleven misfortunes.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 11.6

item.title: There are these five dangers, bhikkhus, for a person without serene confidence. What five? Those without faith are not inspired; some who have faith may…
item.description:
There are these five dangers, bhikkhus, for a person without serene confidence. What five? Those without faith are not inspired; some who have faith may change; he does not follow the Teacher's instruction; later generations follow wrong view; his mind is not serene. Bhikkhus, these are the five dangers for a person without serene confidence.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.218

item.title: Great King, just as a man with a multi-storied mansion with an upper terrace at a crossroads, standing there, would see people entering houses, leaving…
item.description:
Great King, just as a man with a multi-storied mansion with an upper terrace at a crossroads, standing there, would see people entering houses, leaving houses, walking back and forth on the road, sitting at the crossroads or on the upper terrace. He would think: 'These people are entering houses, these are leaving houses, these are walking back and forth on the road, these are sitting at the crossroads, on the upper terrace.' So too, Great King, with his mind thus concentrated, purified, bright, unblemished, free from defilements, pliant, workable, steady, and imperturbable, the bhikkhu directs his mind to the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings. With the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees beings passing away and being reborn.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 2 – Sāmaññaphalasutta

item.title: Here, friends, greed is an unwholesome state, and hatred is also an unwholesome state. There is a Middle Way that abandons greed and abandons hatred,…
item.description:
Here, friends, greed is an unwholesome state, and hatred is also an unwholesome state. There is a Middle Way that abandons greed and abandons hatred, giving rise to (pure) vision, giving rise to (true) knowledge, leading to peace, direct knowledge, enlightenment, Nibbāna. And what, friends, is that Middle Way — (the way) that gives rise to (pure) vision, gives rise to (true) knowledge, leading to peace, direct knowledge, enlightenment, Nibbāna? It is the Noble Eightfold Path, namely: Right View, Right Intention, Right Speech, Right Action, Right Livelihood, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, Right Concentration. Friends, this is that Middle Way, giving rise to (pure) vision, giving rise to (true) knowledge, leading to peace, direct knowledge, enlightenment, Nibbāna.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 3 – Dhammadāyādasutta

item.title: Thus Samaṇa Gotama unites those who are divided, encourages those who are united, delights in harmony, rejoices in harmony, speaks words that lead to harmony.…
item.description:
Thus Samaṇa Gotama unites those who are divided, encourages those who are united, delights in harmony, rejoices in harmony, speaks words that lead to harmony. Bhikkhus, Samaṇa Gotama abstains from harsh speech, avoids harsh speech; he speaks words that are blameless, pleasing to the ear, affectionate, touching the heart, courteous, delightful to many, agreeable to many. Samaṇa Gotama speaks such words.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 1 – Brahmajālasutta

item.title: So too, bhikkhus, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, in accordance with Dhamma, the Dhamma-King, relying on Dhamma, honoring Dhamma, respecting Dhamma, venerating…
item.description:
So too, bhikkhus, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, in accordance with Dhamma, the Dhamma-King, relying on Dhamma, honoring Dhamma, respecting Dhamma, venerating Dhamma, having Dhamma as his banner, having Dhamma as his flag, having Dhamma as his supremacy, gives protection, shelter, and support in accordance with Dhamma regarding bodily action, thinking: 'Such bodily action should be practiced, such bodily action should not be practiced.' Furthermore, bhikkhus, the Tathāgata... gives protection, shelter, and support in accordance with Dhamma regarding verbal action, thinking: 'Such verbal action should be practiced, such verbal action should not be practiced'; regarding mental action, thinking: 'Such mental action should be practiced, such mental action should not be practiced.' That Tathāgata... having given protection, shelter, and support... regarding bodily action, verbal action, mental action, sets in motion the wheel of Dhamma. That wheel is not to be turned back by any ascetic, brahmin, deva, Māra, Brahmā, or anyone in the world.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.14
